Can an Indian company be an authorised CBAM declarant?

No. The status is granted only to a company established in an EU country, by that country's authority. You can register your plant in the CBAM Registry as an operator so declarants can see your verified figures, but that does not make you a declarant.
Does my Indian company need to register for CBAM?
No. Declarant registration is for EU importers. Registering your plant as an operator is optional. It helps when you sell to several EU buyers and are tired of sending each one the same figures.
How do I check my EU buyer has the status?
There is no public register. Ask for their CBAM account number and the EU country that authorised them, and write the duty to hold the status into your contract.

Do our actual emissions need to be verified?

Yes. Actual values in a declaration must be verified by an accredited CBAM verifier. Default values need no verification, but carry a mark-up of 10% in 2026, 20% in 2027 and 30% from 2028. Fertilisers carry 1% instead.

Is a green loan cheaper than a normal loan?

Sometimes, not always. Some schemes cut the cost, like ADEETIE's interest cut, but the rate still rests mostly on your repayment record, cash flow and collateral. Treat any saving as possible, not promised.
My unit is not in an ADEETIE cluster. What now?
BEE says a second phase is planned for about 100 more clusters. Until then, look at SIDBI's energy efficiency loans and your state's efficiency schemes.
Can I combine two schemes on one project?

Sometimes. A unit may get an audit under one programme and the loan from another, but check each scheme's rules before assuming they stack. Tell the bank about any subsidy, and count the energy saving once.
Do I need collateral for a green loan?

Not always. Banks are told not to take collateral from micro and small enterprises for loans up to ₹20 lakh sanctioned from 1 April 2026, and CGTMSE cover can go up to ₹10 crore. Taking that cover is the bank's choice.

Burning a fuel releases carbon dioxide, a little methane and a little nitrous oxide. Background on where a combustion factor comes from. Carbon is conserved: the carbon in the fuel (CC, kilograms of carbon per unit of fuel) that actually burns (OF, the oxidation fraction) leaves as CO₂. Freight is measured in tonne-kilometres: the mass moved (m, kilograms, divided by 1000 to get tonnes) times the distance (d, kilometres). Moving 30,000 kg over 1,400 km is 30 × 1,400 = 42,000 tonne-kilometres. At an illustrative 0.05 kgCO₂e per tonne-kilometre that is 2,100 kgCO₂e.

LPG has a default carbon content of 17.2 kg of carbon per gigajoule.
By equation (3), with full oxidation as the IPCC defaults assume, that is 17.2 × 44/12 ≈ 63.1 kg CO₂ per gigajoule, the tabulated 63,100 kg per terajoule.

5.1 How the language model is constrained
A language model writes its answer one token (a word fragment) at a time.
At each step it scores every possible next token, P(v | everything so far).
At temperature 0 it always takes the highest-scoring token (argmax) instead of sampling at random, which removes sampling randomness.
This lowers variability but does not guarantee identical text across model versions or hardware, which is why results are stored and reused.
The reply must fit a fixed schema of named fields, and a field that is not clearly visible must be null.
The model's output is treated as untrusted input: every field must pass the checks below before it reaches a calculation.
A consistency check on every invoice line: quantity (q) times unit rate (r) should equal the printed line amount (a), apart from rounding.
Printed numbers are rounded, so the allowed gap τ is not a guess.
It is the largest error that rounding alone could cause: a value printed with d decimals can be off by up to half of the last digit, and the rate's error is multiplied by the quantity and vice versa.
